newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Prince, Jackson take stake in entertainment group.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Prince, Jackson take stake in entertainment group.

text.p: Saudi billionaire investor Prince al-Waleed bin Talal and Kingdom Entertainment, the company he jointly owns with U.S. pop star Michael Jackson, said Tuesday they bought 50 percent of Hollywood's Landmark Entertainment Group.

"With the prince's involvement, Landmark Entertainment Group will immediately expand its motion picture, television and live entertainment activities, while at the same time building its theme park and attraction division into an even greater force," a statement issued by the prince's Riyadh office said.
It did not give a value and company officials were not available for comment.
Design and production firm Landmark has created several theme parks around the world and produced special format motion pictures and television productions.
Prince Al-Waleed has built a multi-billion dollar business with interests in construction, real estate, banking, travel, broadcast media, supermarkets and other sectors.

He heads the United Saudi Commercial Bank and has made substantial investments in Citicorp, Euro Disney SCA, Canary Wharf in London's Docklands, U.S. retail group Saks Fifth Avenue and the Plaza Hotel in New York City.
